screening.postureOff: Everything from a sender you've written to reaches your Ohbox, promotions included.
screening.autoApplyTitle: File obvious bulk out of my Screener for me
screening.autoApplyDescription: When a first-time sender is plainly a newsletter or a receipt, file it to Reads or Receipts instead of holding it for you. Deterministic rules only — no AI, and it never spends. Security codes and other sensitive mail are never moved, and first-time people always wait for you. You can move anything back; nothing is deleted. Off by default.

images.microcopy: Either way, images come through our proxy, so a sender never sees your address — and a tracking pixel is never fetched at all.

autoUnsub.title: Unsubscribe when I screen out or mark spam
autoUnsub.on: Screening a sender out also sends their unsubscribe, where they offer one-click.
autoUnsub.off: Their mail is filed and nothing is sent.
autoUnsub.microcopy: One request per list, once, from our servers — so your address and reading times stay out of the sender's log. Senders who offer no one-click link are filed and nothing is sent for them, and a request already sent cannot be taken back.

about.p1: A demo mailbox, invented for it — nobody real, nothing real. Every key and every click works, and none of it leaves this tab: there is no network here at all.
about.p2: The Screener holds first-time senders until you decide. One click files a sender to Ohbox, Reads or Receipts — the ✓ half also marks the held mail read — and the decision becomes a rule for future mail. Reads and Receipts share a skim stream where scrolling past an item marks it seen at the waterline. Tags group messages across views without moving them.

inplace.title: Your server. Your folders. Organized.
inplace.body: ohmail works on the mailboxes you already have — Metanet, Infomaniak, iCloud, Gmail, Outlook, any IMAP server. It organizes them in place: real folders on your real server, readable by any other client, forever.
inplace.compare: Where HEY and Superhuman ask you to move in with them, ohmail works where you already live.
inplace.promise: Leave anytime — your mailbox stays organized.

ai.title: AI proposes. You decide.
ai.body: Rules run first and do the bulk of the work with no AI at all — the design goal is that most of your mail is filed deterministically, by rules you can read and change. Where judgment actually helps, ohmail offers something: a door for a new sender, a draft in your voice, a nudge for a thread that went quiet. Every one of them waits for your yes, and nothing ever sends itself.
ai.status: The AI features are built and tested against the model port. A live model has run in production once — on 3 August 2026 it classified 183 messages from the founder's own mailbox, and every result is still waiting to be reviewed rather than applied. No other account's mail has been sent to it. The managed AI actions switch on with the beta, and the metering and spend limits that govern them are already in place.
ai.toggleBody: This is the same mail, twice. Flip the switch — nothing breaks, nothing goes missing. That is the point: ohmail is a complete mail client with the AI switched off, and a faster one with it on.
ai.captionOn: Suggestions and drafts — proposed, never performed.
ai.captionOff: Rules only. Same mail, same folders, nothing missing.
ai.rowNewOnLine: Suggested from how you handled her studio before. Press ↵ to accept.
ai.rowNewOffLine: Waiting for you — pick a door.
ai.rowReplyDraft: Ciao Giulia, perfetto — il 4 agosto va benissimo. La consegna resta all’atelier, come sempre. Grazie mille!
ai.rowReplyOnLine: Sits in the composer as a proposal. You send it, or you rewrite it, or you delete it.
ai.rowReplyOffLine: Reply — a blank composer, exactly like every other mail app.
ai.rowCodeLine: You see it in full; the code is stripped before AI reads it — in either state. Structural, not a setting.
ai.rowRuleLine: Filed by rule: list header, known newsletter. No AI in either state.
ai.pointGrad: Decide the same way three times and ohmail asks to make it a rule. You approve it once — from then on it runs deterministically, with no AI at all.
ai.pointOtp: When mail carries a verification code or login link, that code is stripped before anything reaches AI, and the mail is never forwarded and never routed automatically — structurally, with no setting to turn it off. You always see the message in full; only what a model would read is stripped.
ai.pointByoTitle: Your key, your machine — or ours
ai.pointByo: On macOS the desktop app runs against your own server — your mail stays on your machine, with no ohmail server in the loop. Pointing its AI at your own API key or a local model is coming next, not wired yet. On Cloud: a monthly bag of AI actions is included, and mail keeps flowing rules-only when it runs out.

fast.title: Fast is a feature.
fast.body: Search answers as you type — typo-tolerant and scoped, over a local mirror of every mailbox — and the rest of the archive is one keystroke further, from the server. Tags instead of folder gymnastics, one tag reaching across every mailbox at once. On the desktop app your mail is already on your machine, so reading and searching work with the wifi off; in the browser that holds for the tab you have open, not for a cold start with no network.
fast.pointB: Tags, not folder trees — across every mailbox
fast.pointC: Desktop reads offline; the browser opens instantly
fast.q1Note: Typos are fine — fuzzy matching, on your own machine.
fast.q2Note: Scope it: from, tag, mailbox, before, has.
fast.q3Note: One tag, every mailbox — no folder gymnastics.

everyday.title: And the rest of the day.
everyday.sub: The parts you stop noticing, which is the point of them.
everyday.pilesBody: Three piles instead of one inbox — and Reads keeps a waterline where you stopped.
everyday.attachmentsBody: Open a PDF or an image inside the message. Everything else downloads, and nothing renders itself.
everyday.trackersBody: A spy pixel is never fetched, so it cannot fire. Ordinary pictures load through our proxy, which hides your address from the sender.
everyday.darkBody: HTML mail adapted to a dark screen, with the sender's original one click away.
everyday.laterBody: Send a message back to tomorrow, to next week, or to a date you pick.
everyday.unsubBody: Screen a newsletter out and ohmail sends the unsubscribe for you, where the sender supports one click.
everyday.writeBody: Reply and forward with Cc and Bcc, from whichever of your mailboxes you choose.
everyday.tagsBody: One tag reaching across every mailbox. Create, rename and delete them in settings.

trial.when: Open now: start today and the fourteen days start with you.
trial.lede: Every tier starts with the whole trial — your own mailboxes, the Screener, real folders, always-on sync, push and the web app. Everything the product does with rules.
trial.terms: It comes with 500 AI actions, so the drafts and the Screener's suggestions are yours to try; the monthly allowance begins when a subscription does. And there is nothing to cancel: give no card, and after fourteen days the trial simply ends.

pricing.title: Desktop is free. The cloud is optional.
pricing.sub: The desktop app is the whole product, free: your mailboxes, your machine, no account and no artificial limits. Cloud is for when you want your mail on your phone, on the web, and organized while you sleep — and it brings a monthly allowance of AI actions with it. Run out and mail keeps flowing rules-only; there are no overage charges, ever. Both are open today, and Cloud starts with fourteen days and no card.
pricing.desktopStatusNote: No telemetry, no analytics. On macOS it is a real mail client: it connects to your own IMAP server and organises your mailbox on your machine, with no ohmail server in the loop — and it can optionally sign in to ohmail Cloud if you want one. Every build makes one signed update check; nothing else leaves your machine on its own.
pricing.desktopD: Reads offline — your mail is already there
pricing.desktopCtaNote: Free — pick your platform below. Every build is the complete app.
pricing.cloudShared: Your mail on the web, and organized while you sleep. The web app, push, always-on processing, AI included — with the mobile apps to follow.
pricing.trialNote: Every tier starts with the 14 days above — no card, and 500 AI actions to try. The monthly allowance begins when the subscription does.
pricing.annualNote: Two months free when billed annually.
pricing.footerLine: You keep your mail either way — it lives on your server, in ordinary folders.

downloads.title: Take it with you.
downloads.sub: One app, three platforms. Free, no account, and it runs on your own machine — sync, rules and search all local, on the mailboxes you already own.
downloads.appleFormat: Disk image · Apple silicon and Intel
downloads.firstRun: The macOS and Windows builds are not signed by Apple or Microsoft yet, so the first launch asks you to confirm it once. Nothing in the app phones home except one signed update check.
downloads.cloudLine: Prefer nothing to install? The web app is live and opens in a browser — it is part of Cloud, along with push and always-on processing. The mobile apps follow.

compare.title: Your mailbox, or theirs.
compare.sub: We like the apps that rethink mail — the ones that screen senders, the ones that add AI to your inbox. They pushed the craft forward and we admire the work. What we don't like is where the organization ends up: inside someone else's app, staying behind when you go. So this table is about one axis only — whose mailbox it is.
compare.addressesUs: Stays exactly where it is — ohmail connects over IMAP
compare.addressesHey: Mail moves to HEY. Your address can come along (HEY for Domains); your existing mailbox can't.
compare.addressesOverlays: Stays put — but only Gmail and Outlook qualify
compare.foldersUs: Real IMAP folders on your server, readable by any client
compare.foldersHey: In HEY's apps only — no IMAP or POP access
compare.foldersOverlays: In their apps and cloud, via provider APIs
compare.leaveHey: Mail exports as one MBOX file; the organization stays behind
compare.leaveOverlays: Some of it syncs back as labels; the rest stays behind
compare.offlineUs: Runs fully on your machine and reads with the wifi off
compare.offlineHey: Native apps, but the service is cloud-only
compare.offlineOverlays: Native apps; processing in their cloud
compare.aiUs: Optional and gated — every suggestion waits for your yes
compare.aiOverlays: Built in, runs in their cloud
compare.note: Compared as of July 2026, from each product's own published documentation. The Superhuman column is being re-checked following Grammarly's acquisition.
compare.usLine: ohmail's answer to every row is the same answer: it's your mailbox. Several of them, in fact — ohmail organizes five, ten, fifty IMAP mailboxes at once, drafts replies in your voice, learns your decisions into rules you can read and change, and never asks you to change your address, your provider, or your other mail apps.
compare.goodwill: These are good products made by people who care about mail. The right model is the one that fits your life, and it may not be ours — that is a fine outcome. We only insist on one thing: the choice should stay yours, and so should the mailbox.

data.title: Where your mail lives.
data.sub: The honest answer is different per tier — so here it is, per tier.
data.desktopBody: Desktop is built so your mail never touches our servers: sync, rules and search all run on your machine. The app is a real mail client — it connects to your own IMAP server and organizes your mailbox locally, with no ohmail server in the loop — on macOS, Windows and Linux alike. Your mail is stored on your own disk, so it is there to read whether or not you have a network.
data.desktopNote: Desktop-only is meant to be a complete way to use ohmail, forever — no account, no cloud, nothing of yours on our side, and not a trial version of anything. If you would rather have a hosted account, the same app can sign in to Cloud instead; that is a choice you make in the app, not a different download.
data.cloudBody: Cloud keeps a full copy of your mail — bodies, headers, subjects and senders, not just metadata — on EU servers, for one purpose: delivering sync, push and search to your devices. Storage is encrypted at rest, connections between your devices and ohmail are encrypted in transit, and your mailbox credentials are additionally encrypted at the application level. It is not end-to-end encrypted — the service has to read mail to file and search it, and a small number of people with production database access could technically read it. Never sold, never mined, never used for anything but serving you. Deleting your account erases that data from live systems immediately and from backups within 30 days. The full privacy policy, naming exactly who can access what, publishes before the first real mailbox connects; the subprocessor and retention list linked in the footer is live today.
data.cloudNote: Why a cloud exists at all: your phone can’t keep a connection to your mailbox open all day — the battery and the operating system won’t allow it. Something has to stay awake to notice new mail and tap you on the shoulder. That is what Cloud is for — push, the web app, and the mobile apps when they land — and doing that job is why it holds a copy of your mail rather than only your rules.
data.aiBody: AI requests go to Anthropic under commercial API terms: your mail is never used to train models, and Anthropic retains requests only briefly under its standard policy (currently up to 30 days). We have not yet negotiated a zero-retention agreement, and we will say so here when we do. Where mail carries a credential — a verification code, a login link, a reset token — the credential is stripped before the request is built, and automatic background routing skips that mail entirely. That's structural, not a setting. A live model has been connected in production exactly once, against the founder's own mailbox; the managed AI actions switch on for everyone with the beta, and the metering and spend limits that govern them are already in place.

faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.q1: What happens to my existing folders?
faq.a1: Nothing destructive. The folders you already have are left exactly as they are; ohmail organizes new mail into real IMAP folders on your server. Everything stays visible to any other mail client, on any device.
faq.a2: Anytime. Your mail never needs exporting — the originals live on your own server, in ordinary folders ohmail created in place, and nothing we do touches them. Be clear about what Cloud holds, though: a full copy of that mail — bodies, headers, subjects and senders — alongside your rules, tags and notes, because that is what makes search and push work. All of it is deleted with your account.
faq.a3: On Cloud: on our servers, within your included actions — that is the part being wired for the beta, and so far a live model has run in production exactly once, on the founder's own mailbox. On Desktop the plan is that you point it wherever you like — your own API key, or a local model so nothing leaves your machine; the app already runs locally against your own server on every platform, and that AI choice is coming next rather than today. Either way, rules with no AI at all run first and are meant to handle most mail — and you can switch the AI off entirely without losing a single feature that files your mail.
faq.q4: What exactly is an AI action?
faq.a4: One unit of AI work: a Screener suggestion for a new sender, a summary, a drafted reply. When your monthly actions run out, mail keeps flowing rules-only until the next cycle. There are no overage charges — ever.
faq.a5: Not as a matter of practice, and our admin tools do not display message content — every response the console can produce is checked by a test that writes a marker into every text column of every table and fails if any of it reaches a staff response. The database itself does not yet refuse those columns to staff tooling: the column-restricted role that would enforce this below the application is built and tested but not yet live, and we will not claim it until it is. The honest fine print: Cloud mail is stored unencrypted at the application level and is not end-to-end encrypted, so someone with production database access could technically read it; that access is held by very few people, and the product privacy policy will spell out who and under what conditions when it publishes, before the first real mailbox connects. On Desktop the question doesn't arise — your mail never reaches our servers at all: the app runs as a real mail client against your own server, on macOS, Windows and Linux alike. Separately, nobody else gets to watch you read either: a spy pixel is never fetched, so it cannot report that you opened anything, and ohmail records who tried. Ordinary pictures do load, through our own proxy, which means the sender's server sees us and never your address.
faq.a6: Any IMAP mailbox: your own domain at Metanet or Infomaniak, iCloud, Gmail, Outlook, a self-hosted server. If it speaks IMAP, ohmail organizes it in place. Native Exchange sync over Microsoft Graph is on the roadmap; Microsoft 365 connects over IMAP, like every other mailbox here.
faq.q7: Is there a trial for Cloud?
faq.a7: Yes — 14 days, no card. It is the whole product: rules, sync, push and the web app all run, and it comes with 500 AI actions so the drafts and the Screener's suggestions are yours to try. Spend those and mail keeps flowing rules-only; the monthly allowance begins when a subscription does. Desktop needs no trial at all; it is simply free.
faq.q8: Desktop or Cloud — what’s the real difference?
faq.a8: The same model, the same vocabulary, and deliberately not the same privacy posture — that is the honest difference. Desktop is free and fully standalone: all processing local, no account, no artificial limits. It is a real mail client on all three platforms — it connects to your own IMAP server and organizes your mailbox on your machine, and because your mail is on your own disk it is there to read with the network down. Your own AI key or a local model is still to come. Cloud adds the web app, push notifications, always-on processing while your computer sleeps, and AI included from $9 a month — and it holds a copy of your mail on our servers to do that. The same download does either one; which door you take is a choice inside the app. Both are open today.

siteScreener.title: You decide who gets in.
siteScreener.body: The first time someone writes to you, they wait at the Screener — not in your inbox. One click picks the door, once, for every mail that sender ever writes: Ohbox for people, Reads for newsletters, Receipts for the paperwork. Or never again — and if it was a newsletter, ohmail can send the unsubscribe on your behalf. Want help deciding? It can suggest a door, at a price you see before you agree to it, and file the obvious ones itself once you switch that on.

screening.unsubFine: One request per list, once, and there is no undo for a request that has been sent.
screening.unsubFineMore: It goes from our servers, never from your browser, so your address and reading times stay out of their logs. Senders with no unsubscribe link are filed and nothing is sent for them.
screening.ruleToggle: Make a rule, so future mail follows
screening.ruleToggleAria: Also make a rule for future mail
screening.footWillRule: This moves the mail that is here, and future mail from {sender} files there too.
screening.footWillRuleDomain: This moves the mail that is here, and future mail from anyone at {domain} files there too.
screening.toastRetargeted: {place} — {count, plural, =0 {their mail is already there} one {1 message from {sender} moved} other {# messages from {sender} moved}}. Their rule now sends future mail there too.
screening.toastAlreadyRuled: {place} — {count, plural, =0 {their mail is already there} one {1 message from {sender} moved} other {# messages from {sender} moved}}. A rule was already sending their future mail there.
screening.toastRuleQueued: {place} — {count, plural, =0 {their mail is already there} one {1 message from {sender} moved} other {# messages from {sender} moved}}. The rule for their future mail will be made when you're back online.
screening.toastRuleFailed: {place} — {count, plural, =0 {their mail did not need moving} one {1 message from {sender} moved} other {# messages from {sender} moved}}, but the rule couldn't be made. Future mail is unchanged.
screening.auditOpen: See all {count, plural, one {1 message} other {# messages}} →
screening.auditAria: Messages from {subject}, and where each one sits
screening.auditCount: {count, plural, one {1 message} other {# messages}} ohmail has synced. Mail still on the server that has not reached us yet is not listed.
screening.auditEmpty: Nothing from this sender has synced yet.

auditWhyRule.sender: A rule you made files mail from {match} into {place}.
auditWhyRule.domain: A rule you made files mail from anyone at {match} into {place}.
auditWhyRule.header: A rule you made on the {match} header files mail into {place}.

screening.auditWhyGate: Waiting at the Screener. Nothing has been decided about this sender yet.
screening.auditWhyArrival: Filed when it arrived. No rule of yours covers it, so something else decided — most often that you had already replied to this sender.
screening.ruleRetro: · applies to the {count, plural, one {1 message} other {# messages}} already here
screening.footWillRuleRetro: Future mail from {sender} files there too, and ohmail applies the rule to the mail already in your mailbox. Messages you have replied to, filed yourself or set aside are left alone. Mail that moves stays moved if you later revoke the rule.
screening.footWillRuleRetroDomain: Future mail from anyone at {domain} files there too, and ohmail applies the rule to the mail already in your mailbox. Messages you have replied to, filed yourself or set aside are left alone. Mail that moves stays moved if you later revoke the rule.

reply.fromSubstituted: {was} is disconnected, so this answers from the address above.
reply.fromSubstitutedUnknown: The address this arrived at is disconnected, so this answers from the address above.
reply.quotedProtected: Verification code — kept out of AI
reply.conversationCount: {count, plural, one {1 message} other {# messages}} on this conversation
reply.statusQueued: Not sent yet. ohmail is still trying.
reply.statusUnverified: We couldn't confirm this send. Check your Sent folder before sending it again.
reply.statusMailboxDisabled: Not sent. That address is disconnected and cannot send.

rules.intro: Every Screener decision writes a rule. These are yours.
rules.empty: No rules yet. Deciding about a sender writes one, and it shows up here.
rules.noCount: Nothing records how many messages a rule has filed, so this page doesn't say.
rules.revokeExplain: This stops the rule deciding new mail. Mail it already filed stays where it is.
rules.retargetExplain: Where new mail matching this rule should go. Mail already filed stays where it is.
rules.toastRevoked: Rule revoked. Your mail hasn't moved.
rules.toastRevokeQueued: Revoke queued — it'll go through when you're back online.
rules.toastRevokeFailed: Couldn't revoke that rule. It's still in place.
rules.toastRetargeted: New mail matching this rule will go to {place}.
rules.toastRetargetQueued: Change queued — it'll go through when you're back online.
rules.toastRetargetFailed: Couldn't change that rule. Nothing has changed.
rules.bulkRevoke: Revoke {count, plural, one {the rule shown} other {all # shown}}
rules.bulkRevokeExplain: This stops {count, plural, one {this rule} other {these # rules}} deciding new mail. Mail it already filed stays where it is.
rules.bulkRevokeConfirm: Revoke {count, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}}
rules.bulkToastRevoked: {count, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}} revoked. Your mail hasn't moved.
rules.bulkToastQueued: Revokes queued — they'll go through when you're back online.
rules.bulkToastPartial: Revoked {ok} of {count}. The rest are still in place.
rules.bulkToastFailed: Couldn't revoke those rules. Nothing has changed.

drafts.title: Drafts
drafts.explainer: Messages you started and haven't sent.
drafts.explainerMore: They're saved to your account, so they're here on every device you read your mail on.
drafts.discardWhat: This deletes the draft. It isn't recoverable, and it's the only copy.
drafts.emptyHint: Start a message and it's saved here after a moment — on this device and every other one.

mailBody.pixelOne: One of them is a tracking pixel.
mailBody.unsupported: Showing the plain-text version of this message.
mailBody.sheetOne: A remote stylesheet was blocked, so this message may look plain.
mailBody.sheetMany: {n} remote stylesheets were blocked, so this message may look plain.
mailBody.oversize: This message's HTML part is too large to render safely. Showing the plain-text version.
mailBody.darkOriginalTitle: Show this message in its original colours
mailBody.darkAdaptTitle: Adapt this message to the dark theme
mailBody.designTitle: Show this message with the sender's own formatting
mailBody.plainTitle: Show this message as text, in the app's own type

attachments.listOffline: Couldn't reach ohmail — check your connection.

attachmentPreview.noPreviewDetail: This kind of file can't be shown here — download it to open.
attachmentPreview.tooLargeDetail: This file is over the fetch limit for on-demand open.
attachmentPreview.pdfErrorDetail: Download it to open in another app.
attachmentPreview.textTruncated: — preview truncated. Download to read the rest.

away.title: Away responder
away.on: On. One reply per person, from the mailbox they wrote to.
away.screenedInNote: Senders still waiting in the Screener are not answered.
away.everyoneNote: Strangers in the Screener are answered too — they learn this address is read.
away.never: Never sent to mailing lists, no-reply addresses, security mail, or your own addresses. Each person is answered once until you change these settings.
away.failed: That did not save. Nothing changed.
away.incomplete: Add a subject and a message before turning this on.
away.unreachable: Your away settings could not be read just now. Nothing here has changed.
away.noticeScreenedIn: Away responder is on — people you've let in get your away note.
away.noticeEveryone: Away responder is on — everyone who writes gets your away note.
